summary: Hard numbers for untrained adults on pulling and arm lifts are scarce in search snippets. Most training studies keep baseline 1RMs in full-text tables that could not be opened. I found no usable untrained 1RM data at all for triceps extension or pushdown, lateral raise, shrug or bent-over row. The pull-up evidence consistently shows that most untrained women cannot do one. Selected, trained female Marines averaged about 1.6 reps in 2011, 55% of female recruits did fewer than 3 after boot camp, and only 4 of 17 normal-weight women managed 1 after 3 months of training. Most young men can do a few, but fewer reach 10: only 22% of a Chinese college sample passed the national standard. A self-report survey claiming 80% of men and 31% of women can do 1+ is probably inflated. NHANES youth data (modified pull-ups: boys 12-15 averaged 9.8, girls 3.7) is the only nationally representative pull-related norm found. The few untrained curl baselines are about 50 lb for a men's machine or preacher-type curl and about 15-17 lb for single dumbbells in a mixed or unknown-sex sample. Novices gain 14-25% on curls and pulldowns within 8-16 weeks, with women gaining more in relative terms. For lat pulldown, untrained men lift about 1.0 x lean body mass (roughly 0.8 x body weight), against about 1.1 x body weight in trained men. Treat everything except the NHANES youth and Senior Fitness Test norms as low-to-medium confidence.
